anna.description: Search Anna's Archive for books and academic articles, get details, or download
anna.template:
Search Anna's Archive for books (incl. audiobooks) and academic articles. Download them. Source repo: https://github.com/jacobhgruber-dev/anna-archive-cli. API key already configured in .env — no setup needed unless binary is missing.

## Setup (run once if binary missing)
If /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/annas-mcp/annas-mcp does not exist:
  git clone https://github.com/jacobhgruber-dev/anna-archive-cli.git /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/annas-mcp
  cd /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/annas-mcp && go build -o annas-mcp ./cmd/annas-mcp
  cp .env.example .env
  mkdir -p /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Anna
  # Then: nano .env to set ANNAS_SECRET_KEY (user already has this)

## Book Search
Run: cd /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/annas-mcp && ./annas-mcp book-search "<query>"
- For audiobooks, include "audiobook mp3 m4b" in the query
- For exact titles, use quotes: "Pride and Prejudice" author name
- Show results in a clean table with #, Title, Author, Format, Size, Hash

## Book Download
When user asks to download a book result, use the hash from the search:
  cd /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/annas-mcp && ./annas-mcp book-download <md5_hash> "Title.ext"
- Extension must match the format from search results (epub, pdf, mp3, m4b, etc.)
- No need to ask for confirmation if the user said "download #3" — just do it
- Downloads go to /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Anna (set in .env)

## Article / Paper Search
Run: cd /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/annas-mcp && ./annas-mcp article-search "<query>"
- Searches Anna's Archive journal content specifically (content=journal in the URL)
- Auto-detects DOIs: if query starts with "10." it does a direct DOI lookup (returns single paper)
- For keyword searches (e.g., "neural networks transformers"), returns multiple results
- Show results in a clean table with #, Title, Authors, Journal, Size, Hash
- If user asks for a paper by DOI, use this command with the DOI

## Article / Paper Download
Run: cd /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/annas-mcp && ./annas-mcp article-download "<doi>"
- Provide the DOI (starts with "10.") from search results or direct lookup
- Tries fast download (API key) first, falls back to SciDB download (no auth needed)
- Downloads go to /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Anna (set in .env)
- No need to ask for confirmation — just download

## Output
Keep results concise: numbered table, basic metadata. Only show download command on request.

audio.description: Search and download audiobooks from AudiobookBay, optionally routed through Tor
audio.template:
Search AudiobookBay for audiobooks and download them via Tor. Downloads go to /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Audio.
Source repo: https://github.com/jacobhgruber-dev/audiobookbay-cli

## Setup (run once if tools are missing)
If python3 can't import requests or bs4: pip3 install --break-system-packages requests beautifulsoup4
If aria2c is not installed: brew install aria2
If torsocks is not installed: brew install torsocks
If /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Audio does not exist: mkdir -p /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Audio

## Tor Check (REQUIRED before any torsocks download)
First verify Tor is running:
  python3 /Users/jacobgruber/.config/opencode/skills/open-tor/scripts/opentor.py check
If Tor is not active, run: brew services start tor
Then verify again before attempting downloads.

## Search
Run: cd /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/audiobookbay-automated && python3 audiobookbay.py search "<query>"
- Always search with max_pages=1 for a fast initial sweep; use max_pages=2 only if user wants more
- Show results in a clean numbered table: #, Title, Format, Bitrate, Size, Posted, Seeds
- Sort by seeds descending when presenting results (best quality first)

## Browse Recent (newly added audiobooks)
Run: cd /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/audiobookbay-automated && python3 -c "
import requests, bs4
r = requests.get('https://audiobookbay.lu/', headers={'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'})
soup = bs4.BeautifulSoup(r.text, 'html.parser')
for i, post in enumerate(soup.select('.post')[:15], 1):
    title = post.select_one('.postTitle a')
    if not title: continue
    meta = post.select_one('.postInfo')
    print(f'{i}. {title.text.strip()[:90]}')
    if meta: print(f'   {meta.text.strip()[:100]}')
    print()
"

## Get Magnet Link
Run: cd /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/audiobookbay-automated && python3 audiobookbay.py magnet "<detail_url>"

## Download via Tor (recommended for privacy)
Verify Tor is active (opentor.py check), then:
  torsocks aria2c --seed-time=0 --bt-require-crypto=true --dir="/Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Audio" "<magnet_link>"

## Download without Tor (faster, less private)
  aria2c --seed-time=0 --bt-require-crypto=true --dir="/Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Audio" "<magnet_link>"

## Notes
- Tor torrent downloads are slower but private. Mention this.
- Present results in a clean table. Sort by seed count highest first.
- Only show magnet/detail links if user asks. Keep output concise.

bay.description: Search and download torrents from The Pirate Bay, YTS (movies), and Nyaa.si (anime/content) — routed through Tor
bay.template:
Search torrents across The Pirate Bay, YTS (movies), and Nyaa.si (anime/content). Download via Tor. Downloads go to /Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Media/Bay.

## Tor Check (REQUIRED before any torsocks download)
First verify Tor is running:
  python3 /Users/jacobgruber/.config/opencode/skills/open-tor/scripts/opentor.py check
If Tor is not active, run: brew services start tor
Then verify again before attempting downloads.

## TPB API Server (start if not running)
Check: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:5050/
If down, start: nohup /Users/jacobgruber/thepiratebay/venv/bin/python3 /Users/jacobgruber/thepiratebay/app.py > /tmp/tpb-api.log 2>&1 &
Wait 2s, then verify.

## TPB Search
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:5050/search/TERM/PAGE/" | python3 -m json.tool
- Page 0 = first 30 results, page 1 = next 30, etc.
- URL-encode spaces as %20
- Sort: curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:5050/search/TERM/0/?sort=seeds_desc"

## TPB Browse by Category
- Top 100 all:              curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/top/0/
- Top 100 Movies:           curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/top/200/
- Top 100 TV:               curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/top/205/
- Top 100 Music:            curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/top/100/
- Top 100 Games:            curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/top/400/
- Top 100 Apps:             curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/top/300/
- Top 100 Audio Books:      curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/top/100/
- Top 48h all:              curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5050/top48h/0/
  Categories: 100=Audio 200=Video 300=Apps 400=Games 600=Other
  Subcategories: 201=Movies 202=Movies DVDR 205=TV

## YTS Movie Search (JSON API, no CF)
curl -s "https://yts.mx/api/v2/list_movies.json?query_term=TERM&limit=10" | python3 -c "
import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin)
for m in d.get('data',{}).get('movies',[]):
    print(f'{m["title"]} ({m["year"]}) | {m.get("rating","?")}/10 | {m.get("runtime","?")}min')
    for t in m.get('torrents',[]):
        print(f'  {t["quality"]} | {t["size"]} | seeds:{t["seeds"]} | peers:{t["peers"]}')
"

## Nyaa.si Search (anime, manga, software — JSON API, no CF)
curl -s "https://nyaa.si/api/search?q=QUERY&limit=10" | python3 -c "
import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin)
for r in d['data']:
    size = r.get('size',0)
    size_str = f'{size/1e9:.1f}GB' if size > 1e9 else f'{size/1e6:.0f}MB'
    print(f'{r["name"][:80]} | {size_str} | seeds:{r["seeders"]} | leech:{r["leechers"]}')
"

## Download (Tor)
Use the "magnet" field from search results.
Verify Tor first, then:
  torsocks aria2c --seed-time=0 --bt-require-crypto=true --dir="/Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Media/Bay" "<magnet>"
Direct (faster, less private):
  aria2c --seed-time=0 --bt-require-crypto=true --dir="/Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Media/Bay" "<magnet>"

## Output
Present results as clean numbered tables: #, Title, Size, Seeds, Leeches, Source (TPB/YTS/Nyaa). If user asks for movies, prefer YTS. If anime, prefer Nyaa. For general searches, default to TPB. Format sizes readable (GB/MB). Don't explain API internals.

blender.description: Open and control Blender via blender-mcp (addon must be running)
blender.template:
Use the blender-mcp MCP tools to control Blender. Load the blender skill first for full context.

## Prerequisites (verify before proceeding)
- Blender is running and the BlenderMCP addon is enabled and connected
- Check: use `get_scene_info` to verify the connection is live

## Available via MCP tools
- get_scene_info, get_object_info, get_viewport_screenshot
- execute_blender_code (full bpy access — save .blend first!)
- Poly Haven: get_polyhaven_categories, search_polyhaven_assets, download_polyhaven_asset, set_texture
- Sketchfab: search_sketchfab_models, download_sketchfab_model
- AI 3D generation: generate_hyper3d_model_via_text/images, generate_hunyuan3d_model, poll jobs, import generated assets

## Headless / batch operations (no GUI needed)
- Run script: /opt/homebrew/bin/blender --background --python script.py
- One-liner: /opt/homebrew/bin/blender --background --python-expr "import bpy; ..."
- Render: /opt/homebrew/bin/blender --background file.blend --render-output /path/ --render-frame 1

## Quick scene creation workflow
1. get_scene_info to see current state
2. Get assets from Poly Haven or Sketchfab if applicable
3. Fall back to execute_blender_code for custom scripting
4. get_viewport_screenshot to verify
5. Save: /opt/homebrew/bin/blender --background current.blend --python-expr "import bpy; bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile()"

Always verify results visually. Z is up in Blender.

transcribe.description: Transcribe audio with whisper (fast) or faster-whisper (high quality)
transcribe.template:
Transcribe the audio file the user provides. Show the full transcript to the user. Save output to ~/Projects/Whisper/output/.

DEFAULT (fast): Use whisper-cli with base.en model:
  whisper-cli -m ~/Projects/Whisper/models/ggml-base.en.bin -f FILE --output-txt --output-srt -l auto -of ~/Projects/Whisper/output/FILENAME
  whisper-cli only supports WAV. If input is M4A/other, convert with ffmpeg first: ffmpeg -i INPUT -ar 16000 -ac 1 -c:a pcm_s16le OUTPUT.wav -y -hide_banner -loglevel error

HIGH QUALITY (when user asks for better accuracy, large-v3, or higher quality): Use faster-whisper via Python venv. Run this single Python script (activate venv inline):
  source ~/Projects/Whisper/fw-env/bin/activate && python3 -c "
  from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
  model = WhisperModel('large-v3', device='auto', compute_type='auto')
  segments, info = model.transcribe('/path/to/file.m4a', beam_size=5, language='en', vad_filter=True)
  txt = []; srt = []; idx = 1
  for seg in segments:
      txt.append(seg.text.strip())
      s, e = int(seg.start), int(seg.end)
      srt.append(f'{idx}\n{s//3600:02d}:{(s%3600)//60:02d}:{s%60:02d},{int((seg.start%1)*1000):03d} --> {e//3600:02d}:{(e%3600)//60:02d}:{e%60:02d},{int((seg.end%1)*1000):03d}\n{seg.text.strip()}\n')
      idx += 1
  with open('/Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Whisper/output/FILENAME.txt','w') as f: f.write('\n'.join(txt))
  with open('/Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Whisper/output/FILENAME.srt','w') as f: f.write(''.join(srt))
  print(f'Saved {len(txt)} segments.')
  "
  Note: `vad_filter=True` prevents hallucination loops. faster-whisper handles M4A/MP3/WAV natively — no ffmpeg conversion needed.

gallery.description: Download entire image galleries from any supported site using gallery-dl
gallery.template:
Use gallery-dl to download image galleries. gallery-dl is installed at /opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl.

## Supported sites (500+)
DeviantArt, Instagram, Twitter/X, Pixiv, Danbooru, Flickr, Imgur, Reddit, ArtStation, Behance, and hundreds more — full list: https://github.com/mikf/gallery-dl/blob/master/docs/supportedsites.md

## Basic download
/opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl "<url>"
- Default: downloads to ./gallery-dl/ in current directory
- Extract archive keeps track of already-downloaded files (no duplicates on re-run)
- Show progress and final count

## Custom output directory
/opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl -d "/Users/jacobgruber/Projects/Media/Galleries" "<url>"

## Download only specific file types
/opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl --filter "extension in ('jpg','png')" "<url>"

## Authentication (for private/protected content)
If user asks for authenticated download from a site:
- Create config: mkdir -p ~/.config/gallery-dl
- Run: /opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl --config-yaml "extractor.<site>.username=<user>" --config-yaml "extractor.<site>.password=<pass>" "<url>"
- OR use cookies: /opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl --cookies ~/Downloads/cookies.txt "<url>"

## Batch / bulk
- Download all galleries from a user: /opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl "<profile_url>"
- Download from a list of URLs (one per line): /opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl -i urls.txt

## Metadata
- Write metadata to JSON: /opt/homebrew/bin/gallery-dl --write-metadata "<url>"

## Options user might want
- --range 1-10 : download first 10 items only
- --abort 3 : skip after 3 consecutive download errors
- --no-part : don't use .part files (no resume support but cleaner)

Always show download progress and final count. Ask about output directory if user hasn't specified one. For large galleries, warn about disk space.

sniff.template:
CRITICAL: The user specified a number of minutes. Use THAT number. Do NOT use 60 or any other default unless the user gave no number.

Run: bash ~/Library/Logs/opencode-capture/analyze.sh <MINUTES_THE_USER_SPECIFIED>
Examples:
  /sniff 5  → bash ~/Library/Logs/opencode-capture/analyze.sh 5
  /sniff 10 → bash ~/Library/Logs/opencode-capture/analyze.sh 10
  /sniff    → bash ~/Library/Logs/opencode-capture/analyze.sh 15

The script takes 20-60 seconds. Wait for the FULL output. Read it silently.

=== OUTPUT RULES ===
- Do NOT show the raw script output to the user. Read it, then produce ONLY the curated report below.
- If the user wants raw output they'll explicitly ask.

=== LANGUAGE RULES (ZERO TOLERANCE) ===
- NEVER say "is" for device identity unless the data proves it. ALWAYS hedge: "likely," "probably," "appears to be."
- NEVER invent device types. If the script says "Unknown," say "Unknown." You may add "possibly a [thing] based on [evidence]" but keep the Unknown label.
- NEVER say "Your MacBook Pro" unless mDNS or hostname literally says "MacBook Pro." Otherwise say "Apple laptop" or "Apple device."

=== REPORT — YOU MUST INCLUDE ALL OF THESE SECTIONS ===

## 📊 Summary
One line: [N] devices on [network], [X] MB transferred, [Y] TLS connections to [Z] unique destinations over [M] minutes.

## 🆕 Surprises
- New devices (from NEW DEVICES section) — what hostname, manufacturer, services do they advertise?
- Domains or external servers you haven't seen before
- Unusually high traffic to anything
- If nothing unusual: "Nothing out of the ordinary — routine traffic."

## 🖥️ Devices
Table: emoji + IP + identity + role + seen time
Example: 💻 .161 — Apple laptop | AirPlay, companion-link | Active all session
Use the raw data (manufacturer, mDNS services, NetBIOS hostnames, DHCP names). Present what the script found as ground truth. Add cautious interpretation: "possibly a Windows laptop based on NetBIOS name"

## 🚦 Activity
Top 5-8 destinations. For each: domain name → connection count → time range → what it probably is (a cautious guess based on the domain name)
Example: calendar.google.com | 520 | 16:12-18:19 | likely Google Calendar syncing

## 🌐 Network
1-2 lines: which network, protocol mix, largest external talker.

## 🟢 System
One line: daemon running/not running.

=== EXAMPLE OF GOOD OUTPUT ===
